component_findings.dependency_metadata: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--quidra): All observed pull requests across quidra-lang/quidra, quidra-lang/dnn, and quidra-lang/vision (core release PR, first-party package compatibility CI PR, and both packages' initial release PRs) are authored and merged by the same single account, koba-jon, who is also recorded as making dnn's and vision's first contributions.
component_findings.distribution_artifacts: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-1--quidra): Package ecosystem activity/maintenance is scored low (15/100). Positive signals exist (recent releases, an explicit cross-repository compatibility CI process, signed/verified release tags, structured versioning against core compatibility ranges), which keep the score above a floor of zero. However the entire observable ecosystem is two packages maintained by a single contributor inside the language's own organization, with zero external stars/forks/independent contributors and only two releases each in a ~48-hour window, so there is essentially no independent community maintenance signal yet. This reflects genuine, verified sparseness rather than missing evidence, so it is scored low rather

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.limitations: Star/fork counts are recorded as declared evidence per the methodology but are explicitly not used as a standalone proxy; they are near-zero for a project this new and are not comparable in scale to established ecosystems for other benchmarked languages.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.selection_rule: Use the primary package registry/ecosystem for the language when one exists and evaluate current observable maintenance within the fixed activity window; package count alone is never sufficient.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.candidate_universe: Fixed checklist of 10 language-neutral library domains evaluated identically for every language in this benchmark run: (1) Web/HTTP server or client framework beyond a bare built-in, (2) Database driver/ORM, (3) Testing framework beyond the language's own built-in assert facility, (4) Serialization beyond built-in JSON, (5) CLI argument-parsing framework beyond a built-in facility, (6) Logging framework, (7) Image/computer-vision processing, (8) Machine learning / deep learning (DNN), (9) Date/time extension beyond built-in, (10) Cryptography/security library.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations: Both discovered packages are maintained inside the same GitHub organization (quidra-lang) that owns the compiler and are described in the language's own docs as 'first-party' rather than independently authored third-party contributions, so even the 2/10 domain coverage found is not evidence of an independent third-party ecosystem. | GitHub star/fork counts were observed (0 stars, 0 forks on all three quidra-lang repositories checked) but are not used as the scoring basis by themselves; they are recorded only as corroborating context per the methodology's restriction on raw popularity proxies.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.selection_rule: Inspect the same five fixed domain groups for every language; prefer the official package index or official ecosystem directory, then independent package/project evidence.
